summary:
Marswalk planning involves balancing terrain hazards, environmental conditions, travel time, and suit resources—information that can be difficult to assess together. Martian Map brings these considerations into one planning interface for astronauts, mission planners, and people exploring Mars mission data. It is a prototype planning aid, not a certified tool for real missions.

We built a browser-based Marswalk planner for Sakarya Vallis in Gale Crater. It uses HiRISE terrain data to show elevation, slope, and roughness, then calculates terrain-aware routes between editable stops. The interface also estimates EVA time and suit consumables, supports emergency-return planning, and displays Curiosity weather, RAD-based radiation estimates, and NASA DONKI space-weather information. These outputs are estimates based on the project’s data and assumptions.

================================================================================

PROJECT SUMMARY

================================================================================

We developed Martian Map, an interactive, offline-ready Marswalk (EVA) planner

built for Sakarya Vallis in Gale Crater (5.08° S, 137.26° E). Addressing the

Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge, the app transforms real

NASA/University of Arizona HiRISE stereo terrain (1 m/px block-averaged to a

10 m grid with metre-scale roughness) into an A* safe-path router that steers

crews away from >=20° cliffs and boulder fields.

Every route edit triggers a live, mission-control style GO / CAUTION / NO-GO

poll across five survival pillars: terrain slope and footing, suit consumables

(O2, cooling water, battery, and Point-of-No-Return margins), Curiosity REMS

weather, Curiosity RAD radiation (0.64 mSv/day), and NASA DONKI solar particle

alerts—paired with interactive dust-storm simulations, Curiosity Mount Sharp

imagery, and emergency abort routing for solo, buddy-pair, or rover-assisted

crews.

Because astronauts cannot eyeball lethal slopes or shifting hazards in a

pressurized suit, Martian Map turns verified NASA, USGS, and university mission

data into fast, life-saving decisions.

================================================================================

PROJECT DETAILS

================================================================================

1. What It Does & How It Works

------------------------------

- Real Terrain & Hazard Grid: A 438 MB, 1 m/px HiRISE stereo DTM

(DTEEC_006855_1750_007501_1750_A01) is pre-processed into a 10 m elevation grid

(sakarya-10m.bin) and a 1 m plane-fit RMS roughness grid

(sakarya-10m-rough.bin) that preserves metre-scale blocks and ledges.

- Hazard-Aware A* Routing: Crew members can drag numbered stops or add new

waypoints. An A* pathfinder routes every leg around terrain >=20° (treated as

impassable walls without corner-cutting), penalizes steep ground (15–20°),

applies a 2x cost to rough ground (>=0.5 m relief) and 6x to boulder fields

(>=1.0 m), and flags any unroutable leg in dashed red.

- Mission-Control GO / CAUTION / NO-GO Poll: Recomputes terrain hazards across

every sampled 10 m cell, suit consumables (1200 L O2, 8 kg cooling water,

1000 Wh battery with 25% reserve) and Point-of-No-Return (PNR) margins,

Curiosity REMS midday air temperatures (with offline bundled fallback),

Curiosity RAD dose (0.64 mSv/day vs. NASA's 600 mSv career limit), NASA DONKI

solar particle events, and an interactive dust optical depth (tau) what-if

slider (Clear, Haze x0.8, Storm x0.5 -> NO-GO).

- Stop Walkthrough & Emergency Abort: Pairs stops with NASA Curiosity Mount

Sharp rock-unit imagery, provides a scrubbable elevation profile synced to a

live map marker, and computes emergency abort routes for a Solo walker,

Buddy pair, or Pair + rover.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

-----------------------------

- Crew Safety: Replaces straight-line guesswork with slope-, roughness-, and

reserve-aware routing before egress and during contingencies.

- Zero-Connectivity Resilience: Runs as an offline-ready Progressive Web App

(sw.js) that precaches terrain grids, overlays, and imagery.

- Educational & Mission Transparency: Clearly separates measured

NASA/USGS/university datasets from explicit engineering assumptions.

3. Tools, Languages & Data Sources

----------------------------------

- Core App: Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, modern ES Module JavaScript (zero-framework,

zero-bundler), Leaflet (EPSG:4326), Service Worker (sw.js).

- Data Processing & Testing: Node.js scripts (tools/build-terrain.mjs,

tools/fetch-rems.mjs) and node:test unit suites.

- AI & Media Tooling: Application code developed with Claude; pitch video and

presentation slides created with Gemini.

- Data Sources:

* HiRISE Stereo DTM & Orthoimage (NASA / JPL / University of Arizona)

* Mars Trek MOLA, THEMIS, Viking & Esri-hosted MRO CTX tiles (NASA / USGS / Esri)

* Curiosity REMS Weather (CAB CSIC-INTA / NASA JPL)

* Curiosity RAD Radiation Dose, Hassler et al. 2014 (0.64 mSv/day)

* NASA DONKI Solar Particle Events & NASA Photojournal (PIA19818, 19912, 19839, 21716)

4. Creativity & Key Design Considerations

-----------------------------------------

- Suit-Glove & High-Stress UI: 44 px touch targets, large tabular numerals, four

focused tabs (Plan, Stop, Environment, Layers), full keyboard navigation, and

colorblind-safe status indicators pairing color with text and shape

(GO, CAUTION, NO-GO).

- Fail-Safe Defaults: Offline or rate-limited DONKI feeds explicitly report

CAUTION rather than silently defaulting to GO.

- Honest Engineering: Stop photos are transparently labeled as Curiosity views

of equivalent Mount Sharp rock units ~15–25 km away, and suit capacities are

documented as planning baselines.
